title: AsyncAPI exporter anchor manifest
description: Schema for analysis/handoff/contracts/asyncapi/anchor_manifest.json produced by skills/asyncapi-from-context/scripts/generate_asyncapi.py (v1.3.1). Extends governance/schemas/sidecar_anchor_manifest.base.schema.json with AsyncAPI-specific discriminators (sidecar literal `asyncapi-from-context`, path extension `\.(yaml|yml|json)$`, view-element-kind enum {Channel, Operation, Message, Server}, format discriminator `asyncapi-3.0`, structured unmapped_anchors array). The exporter is operator-driven (NOT a sidecar in the orchestrator-detection sense), but reuses the sidecar manifest base shape so downstream tooling that reads sidecar manifests can also read this exporter's manifest without special-casing. F5 does NOT validate this schema (the exporter writes operator-side artifacts under analysis/handoff/, not canonical state); the schema is consumed by tests/test_generate_asyncapi.py and by future downstream consumers that want to verify exporter output before shipping. Mirrors v1.3.0 openapi-from-context schema with AsyncAPI-shape adjustments (Channel instead of PathItem, format const asyncapi-3.0 instead of openapi-3.1, channel-collision reason instead of path-collision).

format.description: Discriminator for spec-version drift. v1.3.1 emits AsyncAPI 3.0 only; future spec-version (3.1, 4.0) bumps would extend the enum.

view_element_id.description: AsyncAPI element identifier. Channel entries use the channel key in the YAML (e.g., `channel_anc_user_signedup_001`); Operation entries use `<action> <channel-key>` (e.g., `send channel_anc_user_signedup_001`); Message entries use `<channel-key>.<message-name>` (reserved for future); Server entries use the server name (reserved for future). v1.3.1 emits Channel + Operation only.

view_element_kind.description: AsyncAPI element kind. v1.3.1 emits Channel + Operation; Message + Server are reserved for future structured-input releases.

notes.description: Optional free-text annotation. Common content: original ClaimID/A51Ref this anchor traces to (mirrored into the AsyncAPI operation's tag); rationale for the channel placeholder when the operator should refine.

anchor_status.description: v1.3.7+: machine-readable promotion status. 'candidate' = exporter produced a v1.3.0+ skeleton placeholder for this anchor (no real payload schemas synthesized — operator must enrich the AsyncAPI before shipping). 'promoted' is reserved for future releases that auto-synthesize real shapes from interface_contract_model.md. v1.3.0..v1.3.6 emitted no anchor_status (legacy consumers should treat absence as 'candidate'); v1.3.7+ emits 'candidate' explicitly so 'this is a skeleton, enrich it' is grep-able from CI / release-readiness gates.

unmapped_anchors.description: A61 anchors that were considered for inclusion but skipped, with structured reasons. Empty when every contract-class anchor produced a channel. Operator-readable signal: 'X anchors couldn't be auto-materialized; review and decide'.

reason.description: Why the anchor was skipped. `non_contract_anchor_class` — AnchorClass != contract (the exporter materializes only contract-class anchors). `element_id_not_channel_shaped` — ElementID doesn't match `^/[A-Za-z0-9_/{}.~-]*$` (ASCII-exact path characters; `%` is intentionally rejected — see exporter docstring), OR has malformed OpenAPI-style template syntax (unbalanced / empty / nested / misordered `{...}`), OR contains a `{...}` template whose name doesn't match the AsyncAPI 3.0 Parameter Object name charset `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (illegal template names like `{tenant.id}`, `{user id}`, `{order/sub}` rejected at the shape gate to keep the brace-balance scan and the `parameters` extractor in atomic agreement; v1.3.1 R2 lesson), OR is a dot-style address like `user.signed_up` (v1.3.1 supports only path-style; dot-style deferred to v1.3.1.x). `element_id_path_traversal` — ElementID contains a literal `..` (encoded variants like `%2e%2e` are blocked by the channel-shape gate above and surface as `element_id_not_channel_shaped`). `duplicate_channel_collision` — two anchors map to the same channel address; first wins, rest skipped.

element_id.description: Optional: the original ElementID, surfaced for operator triage.
